module: List of objects ordered by `sortOrder`, with an index by id (objects) and by name (byName). It builds objects through a provided constructor, and handles sorting, moving, serialization and debug drawing. The module returns a list constructor; it is used for gameplay editor collections (sites, zones, etc.).
usage:
local liste = require("gameplay/util/sortedList")("zones", parent, function(parent, name, forceId) return maClasse(parent, name, forceId) end)
local obj = liste:create("zone1")
liste:buildNamesDir()
notes: Created objects must have id, name, sortOrder, drawDebug(), onSerialize() and onDeserialized().
objects has a metatable: reading a nonexistent id returns {name = "Missing!", missing = true, id = -1} instead of nil.
byName is only updated by buildNamesDir(); in case of duplicate names, the first sorted object wins.
create() forces obj.isProcedural = false; only non-procedural objects are serialized.
In onDeserialized, old ids are recorded in oldIdMap[oldId] = new id.
The postClear, postRemove and postCreate hooks default to nop and can be replaced on the instance.

C.desc: Ordered list. Fields: name, parent, objectConstructor, objects (id -> object), sorted (sorted array), byName.

parent.desc: Parent object passed to the element constructor.

objectConstructor.desc: function(parent, name, forceId) returning a new element.

clear.desc: Clears the list (objects, sorted, byName) then calls postClear.

create.desc: Creates an element via objectConstructor, registers it and re-sorts (unless skipSort), then calls postCreate.

skipSort.desc: Do not re-sort (useful for batch creation).

remove.desc: Removes an element (object or id), re-sorts then calls postRemove.

sort.desc: Rebuilds sorted according to sortOrder and renumbers sortOrder from 1 to N.

move.desc: Swaps an element's position with its neighbor in the given direction.

dir.desc: -1 toward the start, +1 toward the end.

onSerialize.desc: Returns the list of serialized non-procedural elements, in order.

onDeserialized.desc: Clears the list and recreates the elements from the data.

oldIdMap.desc: Table filled with old id -> new id.
